Name: Strangler Fig
Strategy: Route selected capabilities through a facade to new services while legacy serves unmigrated functionality
Risk: Medium - cross-system dependencies and facade bottlenecks
Rollback Plan: Revert capability routing only while legacy code and data remain compatible and current; otherwise restore objects and replay changes
Duration Estimate: Scope-dependent; plan and validate one capability at a time
Gotcha: Define data ownership and cross-system adapters; retire legacy objects only after validation and an explicit rollback window

Name: Dual Write
Strategy: Update two stores during migration; prefer a source transaction plus outbox or CDC for asynchronous propagation
Risk: High - independent writes can partially fail or be reordered
Rollback Plan: Keep old store authoritative before cutover; stop target writes and reconcile; after cutover recover target-only writes before reverting
Duration Estimate: Workload-dependent; measure propagation and reconciliation time
Gotcha: Outbox atomically records source changes and publish intent; it does not atomically commit both stores; use idempotent consumers and preserve required ordering

Name: Change Data Capture (CDC)
Strategy: Take a consistent snapshot then stream source log changes to the target with durable offsets
Risk: Medium - asynchronous lag; recovery duplicates; retention gaps and incompatible schemas
Rollback Plan: Before cutover retain source authority; pause target use and repair or resnapshot; stopping capture alone is not rollback
Gotcha: Debezium PostgreSQL can redeliver after failure; use idempotent sinks and monitor applied offsets plus WAL retention; it does not emit DDL change events

Name: Expand-Contract Schema
Strategy: Add compatible columns/tables; backfill and migrate readers and writers; remove old fields after the rollback window
Risk: Medium - compatibility depends on application versions and data mapping; contraction can destroy data
Rollback Plan: Before contraction revert code only while old fields remain current; after contraction restore or reconstruct data with a tested migration
Duration Estimate: Deployment-dependent; stage expansion and contraction separately
Gotcha: Adding a dropped column does not restore its values; verify old/new readers and writers and backfill correctness before removing old fields

Name: Blue-Green Database
Strategy: Replicate blue into green; validate green; fence writes and catch up before switching endpoints
Risk: Medium-High - switchover interrupts connections and writes; green can diverge after promotion
Rollback Plan: Abort before promotion on failed checks; after promotion reconcile new writes before any return to blue
Duration Estimate: Workload-dependent; rehearse sync and switchover timeout
Gotcha: RDS stops replication between environments after switchover; retained blue is not an automatically current rollback target; test reconnects and DNS caching

Name: Parallel Run
Strategy: Compare old and new read results on sampled traffic while returning the old result
Risk: Medium - shadow work adds load and latency; mutations can duplicate side effects
Rollback Plan: Disable shadow evaluation while keeping the control path active; investigate any side effects already produced
Duration Estimate: Workload-dependent; collect representative traffic and mismatch evidence
Gotcha: Use read-only or isolated candidates; normalize only understood differences; concurrent data changes can create false mismatches and synchronous candidates can time out

Name: Trickle Migration
Strategy: Copy resumable primary-key chunks while capturing concurrent changes; resolve snapshot/stream collisions
Risk: Medium - stale backfill can overwrite newer changes; copying competes with production load
Rollback Plan: Before cutover keep source authoritative; pause copy and resume from durable progress after reconciling affected keys
Duration Estimate: Workload-dependent; benchmark chunks and catch-up under production load
Gotcha: Debezium incremental snapshots use watermarks to resolve concurrent updates/deletes; PostgreSQL connector does not support schema changes during an incremental snapshot

Name: Feature Flag Migration
Strategy: Roll out cohorts through explicit read/write stages and compare consistency before changing the authoritative system
Risk: Medium - flags control routing but do not make dual writes atomic or restore data
Rollback Plan: Return to a prior stage only while its code and data are usable; after new-only writes reconcile old data before reverting
Duration Estimate: Workload-dependent; gate each stage on consistency and performance
Gotcha: Keep rollback writes until the rollback window closes; flag propagation is not a global transaction; remove temporary flags after completion

Name: API Version Migration
Strategy: Support old and new versions during a communicated transition period; test consumer compatibility before retiring old endpoints
Risk: Medium - version coexistence adds compatibility testing and support obligations
Rollback Plan: Extend old-version support when needed; verify old handlers can represent current stored data before reverting clients
Duration Estimate: Consumer-dependent; use published support policy and adoption evidence
Gotcha: Deprecation signals lifecycle status rather than shutdown; use RFC 9745 Deprecation and migration links when applicable and RFC 8594 Sunset for planned unavailability

Name: Zero-Downtime Cutover
Strategy: Target minimal interruption; fence old writers and drain in-flight work; verify catch-up before moving traffic
Risk: High - DNS changes are not atomic; write pauses and reconnects may be visible
Rollback Plan: Abort before new writes if acceptance checks fail; after new writes require tested reverse replication or reconciliation before returning traffic
Duration Estimate: Workload-dependent; rehearse and set an explicit abort timeout
Gotcha: Zero downtime is a goal rather than a guarantee; RDS switchover drops connections and pauses writes; test retries without duplicating side effects

Name: Database Sharding Migration
Strategy: Copy and replicate into target shards; validate data with VDiff in Vitess; switch traffic with catch-up checks
Risk: High - query locality and ID generation can change; write cutover can pause or reject writes
Rollback Plan: In Vitess retain healthy reverse replication and use ReverseTraffic before Complete; changing a shard map alone does not recover writes
Duration Estimate: Workload-dependent; benchmark copy and cutover with lag limits
Gotcha: Choose shard keys for query and transaction locality; Vitess Complete removes replication artifacts and by default source tables; retain them through the rollback window

Name: Monolith Decomposition
Strategy: Extract vertical business capabilities with explicit data ownership and independently deployable interfaces
Risk: High - shared data and transactional dependencies can become distributed coupling
Rollback Plan: Keep a tested legacy path during transition; revert only with compatible synchronized data or a tested recovery migration
Gotcha: Start with manageable capabilities to establish operational readiness; decouple data with the capability rather than mandating database-first extraction

Name: Cloud Provider Migration
Strategy: Assess workloads and dependencies; choose rehost/replatform/refactor per workload; establish target foundations before deployment
Risk: High - service compatibility and identity/network dependencies vary by workload
Rollback Plan: Retain source capacity during validation; return traffic only if source data and dependencies are still usable; reconcile new writes otherwise
Duration Estimate: Scope-dependent; estimate from inventory and performance benchmarks
Gotcha: Validate service semantics and data transfer requirements individually; do not assume managed-service equivalence or that shared IaC tooling makes providers interchangeable

Name: Queue/Broker Migration
Strategy: Stage target topology and clients; transfer or drain backlog with a tested bridge; coordinate producer and consumer cutover
Risk: High - transfer can reorder or redeliver messages; protocol and acknowledgement semantics may differ
Rollback Plan: Before retiring old broker retain backlog accounting; returning consumers requires recovering target-only messages and preventing duplicate side effects
Duration Estimate: Workload-dependent; measure backlog drain and client rollout
Gotcha: RabbitMQ blue-green uses definitions import and federation; concurrent shovel/federation can reorder messages; cross-product schema and offset portability requires separate verification

Name: Kubernetes Migration
Strategy: Move workloads incrementally; use Deployments for stateless replicas and StatefulSets where stable identity/storage is required
Risk: Medium-High - storage provisioning and application recovery need explicit design
Rollback Plan: Keep previous runtime during validation; return traffic only after ensuring compatible current data; workload rollout undo does not restore database contents
Duration Estimate: Workload-dependent; validate storage and recovery before scheduling cutover
Gotcha: StatefulSets support stateful workloads but do not replace backup/replication plans; check PVC retention policy and rehearse failed OrderedReady rollout recovery

Name: Migration Data Validation Gate
Strategy: Compare source and target rows after load and during CDC; resolve mismatches and unvalidated records before cutover
Risk: Medium - validation adds load and moving records can yield incomplete comparisons
Rollback Plan: Hold cutover with source authoritative; repair or reload affected data and rerun validation
Duration Estimate: Data-dependent; budget validation time in addition to transfer
Gotcha: AWS DMS requires supported keys and endpoints; check pending/suspended/failed counts and excluded columns; zero failures alone does not establish completeness

Name: Online Index Migration
Strategy: For PostgreSQL use CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY where supported; monitor progress and verify index validity before relying on it
Risk: Medium - concurrent builds add CPU/I/O and wait for transactions; failed builds can leave invalid indexes
Rollback Plan: Inspect failed artifacts; drop the invalid index and retry or use supported concurrent reindex; preserve indexes required by existing code
Duration Estimate: Table/workload-dependent; rehearse scans and transaction waits
Gotcha: CONCURRENTLY cannot run inside a transaction block; only one concurrent build per table; an invalid unique index can still enforce uniqueness

Name: Logical Replication Cutover Readiness
Strategy: For PostgreSQL coordinate subscriber schema changes and sequence values before promotion; inventory objects outside logical replication
Risk: High - row catch-up does not prove schema or sequence readiness; missing objects can break promoted writes
Rollback Plan: Keep publisher authoritative until readiness passes; after promotion reconcile subscriber writes before reverting
Duration Estimate: Schema/workload-dependent; rehearse object checks and promotion
Gotcha: PostgreSQL 18 does not logically replicate DDL or sequence state or large objects; apply compatible additive DDL on subscriber first and advance sequences safely before new writes
